issues.legal_issue: Credible testimony corroborated by recovery of marked currency can support a conviction, and concurrent factual findings are not disturbed in an appeal by special leave without sufficient justification.
material_facts: The complainant testified that the accused demanded money to correct an official land-cultivation entry and that he handed the accused the agreed sum.
The marked currency notes were recovered from the accused’s clothing shortly after the payment.
The accused claimed that the complainant had forcibly placed the notes in his pocket; the trial court and High Court disbelieved that account and made concurrent findings against him.
issues.conclusion: The evidence supported the finding that the accused received the money as illegal gratification, and the Court declined to interfere with the concurrent findings in the appeal by special leave.
issues.legal_principle: In an appeal under Article 136 of the Constitution, the Supreme Court would not interfere with concurrent factual findings where the evidence supports them and there is no justification for doing so. The testimony about payment, corroborated by recovery of the marked notes, supported the finding of receipt; the account that the notes were forcibly placed in the accused’s pocket was properly disbelieved.

rule.if: special_leave_appeal_from_conviction and concurrent_findings_against_accused and witness_testified_to_illicit_payment and marked_money_recovered_from_accused and forcible_placement_account_disbelieved

predicates.special_leave_appeal_from_conviction: The accused brought an appeal by special leave challenging a conviction.
predicates.concurrent_findings_against_accused: The trial court and the appellate court both found against the accused on the relevant facts.
predicates.witness_testified_to_illicit_payment: A witness testified that the accused received money in exchange for performing an official act.
predicates.marked_money_recovered_from_accused: Currency previously identified by investigators was recovered from the accused after the alleged payment.
predicates.forcible_placement_account_disbelieved: The courts rejected the accused’s account that another person forcibly placed the money on him.

issues.definition: When an accused challenges a conviction by special-leave appeal, supported concurrent findings based on testimony of illicit payment and recovery of marked money are upheld where the forcible-placement account has been disbelieved.

issues.legal_issue: An irregularity in the authority of an investigator does not invalidate a trial or conviction unless the accused was prejudiced by it.
material_facts: The accused contended that the police officer who investigated the case was not authorized to do so.
The High Court rejected the contention, and the Supreme Court accepted that any investigation irregularity did not vitiate the trial or conviction in the absence of evidence of prejudice.
issues.conclusion: Even if there was an irregularity in the investigation, it did not invalidate the trial or conviction because prejudice to the accused was not shown.
issues.legal_principle: An irregularity in an investigation does not, by itself, vitiate the trial or conviction; prejudice to the accused must be shown. The Court applied this principle while considering the challenge to the investigation in the criminal appeal.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_challenging_conviction and investigation_authority_challenged and investigation_irregularity_assumed and prejudice_not_shown

predicates.criminal_appeal_challenging_conviction: The accused brought a criminal appeal challenging a conviction.
predicates.investigation_authority_challenged: The accused contended that the investigating officer lacked authority to investigate.
predicates.investigation_irregularity_assumed: An irregularity in the investigation is assumed for the purpose of deciding its effect on the trial.
predicates.prejudice_not_shown: The accused did not establish that the investigation irregularity caused prejudice.

issues.definition: When a conviction is challenged on the basis of an assumed investigation irregularity, the trial and conviction are not invalidated if the accused has not shown prejudice.

issues.legal_issue: A prolonged period on bail, together with punishment already served and the passage of time since the offence, may justify reducing a sentence where the governing sentencing law permits a lesser sentence for recorded reasons.
material_facts: The accused had already undergone more than six months of imprisonment.
He had remained on bail for a substantial period after leave to appeal was granted.
Several years had passed since the offence.
The Court relied on the principle in Jagdish Prasad v. State of West Bengal that a prolonged period on bail may be relevant when the court has discretion to impose a lesser sentence for reasons.
issues.conclusion: The Court confirmed the conviction but reduced the sentence to the period of imprisonment already undergone.
issues.legal_principle: Where the governing sentencing law permits a court to impose a sentence below a prescribed minimum for reasons to be given, a prolonged period on bail is a relevant consideration in exercising that discretion. The Court relied on Jagdish Prasad v. State of West Bengal and considered the imprisonment already undergone and the time elapsed since the offence.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_including_sentence_review and sentence_law_allows_lesser_sentence_for_reasons and substantial_imprisonment_already_served and prolonged_period_on_bail and substantial_time_since_offence

predicates.criminal_appeal_including_sentence_revie: The accused brought a criminal appeal in which the sentence was before the court for review.
predicates.sentence_law_allows_lesser_sentence_for_: The applicable sentencing framework permits a court to impose a lesser sentence if it gives reasons.
predicates.substantial_imprisonment_already_served: The accused had already served a substantial part of the custodial sentence.
predicates.prolonged_period_on_bail: The accused had remained on bail for a substantial period while the appeal was pending.
predicates.substantial_time_since_offence: A substantial period had elapsed since the offence was committed.

issues.definition: Where a criminal appeal permits review of the sentence, a substantial period already served, a prolonged period on bail, and substantial time since the offence may justify reducing the sentence to the time already served if the sentencing framework permits a lesser sentence for reasons.
